masteryZone.q: Which of the following describes the difference between the vows of monks (Mahavratas) and lay followers (Anuvratas)?
opts: Monks only practice Ahimsa and Satya, while householders practice all five vows.
Monks observe the vows absolutely and strictly, while householders practice a modified, milder form of the same vows to accommodate daily life.
Householders must renounce all their property, while monks are allowed to hold material assets.
The two systems are completely unrelated and do not share any common vows.
masteryZone.sol: Monks practice the vows strictly (Mahavrata), while householders practice them in a milder form (Anuvrata) to balance spiritual growth with family and societal duties.

masteryZone.q: Vardhamana Mahavira added the vow of Aparigraha (non-possession) to Jainism.
opts: True
False
masteryZone.sol: False. Aparigraha was already one of the four vows of Parshvanatha. Mahavira added the fifth vow, Brahmacharya (chastity).

masteryZone.q: In Jain philosophy, the actual physical, material particles that float in the universe and bind to the soul are called _________.
opts: Jiva
Pudgala
Niyati
Siddha
masteryZone.sol: karmic matter is considered physical particles called Pudgala.

masteryZone.q:
Match the karmic stages with their definitions:
1. Asrava -> Influx of Karma
2. Bandha -> Bondage of Karma
3. Samvara -> Stoppage of Karma
4. Nirjara -> Shedding of Karma
opts: All are correctly matched
Only 1 and 2 are correct
Only 3 and 4 are correct
None of the matches are correct
masteryZone.sol: All of them are correctly matched in sequence.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Vardhamana Mahavira and his followers rejected the authority of the Vedas.
Reason (R): Jains rejected the Vedic class structure and the efficacy of sacrifices, arguing that liberation depends on conduct rather than rituals.
Select the correct option:
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A. The rejection of Vedas was driven by opposition to ritual sacrifices and birth-based social hierarchies.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Jain metaphysics:
1. Anekantavada asserts that reality has manifold aspects.
2. Syadvada is the epistemological method of expressing relativity using Saptabhangi Naya.
Which of the statement(s) is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are correct. Anekantavada is the metaphysical theory, and Syadvada is its epistemological expression.

masteryZone.q: Why does Jainism place a extreme emphasis on the practice of Ahimsa, even extending it to inanimate elements like rocks and wind?
opts: Because they believe that conscious souls (Jivas) exist in all natural elements, and causing harm to them generates negative karma.
To attract people living in forest areas to join the monastic order.
To prevent the development of mining and metallurgy in ancient Magadha.
Because the contemporary kings demanded it to reduce warfare.
masteryZone.sol: Jain animism holds that Jivas are present in all natural objects (earth-bodied, water-bodied, fire-bodied, etc.), so hurting any element of nature accumulates bad karma.

masteryZone.q: How does a Jain soul achieve complete liberation (Moksha) under Mahavira's teachings?
opts: By performing Vedic sacrificial fires (Yajnas) to please the Gods.
By stopping the influx of new karma (Samvara) and shedding all accumulated karma (Nirjara) through severe penance.
By meditating on a single personal deity (Bhakti).
By declaring that the soul does not exist.
masteryZone.sol: Moksha is attained through the combination of Samvara (stopping new karma) and Nirjara (burning off old karma) through rigorous self-discipline.
